title: Edges
description: How one item links to another, how to choose an edge type, and what the bin does across a link.
job: A builder learns how items link, how to choose an edge type, and what the bin does across a link.
kind: concept
---

An **edge** links one item to another: it points **from** one item **to** another, such as a comment to the lease it's about. It's a record of its own, with an `id`, properties and a [version](/build/versions), so **writing an edge never moves either item's version.**

<Terminal>

```bash
marfa edges create --from-id 01a1fc3e-34fa-7062-8de7-da8fc361f12c --to-id 01a1fc3e-34ea-7771-b388-9b9b48bfd87c --type comments-on
```

```text
linked 01a1fc3e-34fa-7062-8de7-da8fc361f12c -> 01a1fc3e-34ea-7771-b388-9b9b48bfd87c with comments-on edge 01a1fc3e-4469-7373-a946-538fc308c747
```

</Terminal>

## Edge types

Every edge has an **edge type**, which sets the rules: which item types each end can be, how many edges an end holds, whether edges can loop, and what the bin does across it. `many-to-one` lets each from item hold at most one edge of the type, so a comment is on one item. `one-to-many` lets each to item hold at most one, so a child has one parent. No edge links an item to itself, and `parent-of` and `supersedes` refuse any loop.

A write that breaks a rule is refused `400 edge_constraint_violation`, or `400 edge_cycle` for a loop. Marfa ships eleven edge types, listed on the Catalog's [Edges](/catalog/edges) page, and a key can [register more](/reference/api/edge-types/registerEdgeType).

### Choose an edge type

Start from what the link means to a person:

- **One item sits under another,** as a subtask under its task: `parent-of`. To gather items without owning them, use `in-collection`.
- **An item exists only for another,** as a comment or a receipt photo: `comments-on` or `attached-to`, which make it a [part](#parts). For one that stands alone, as a note about a film, use `about`.
- **A message belongs to a thread:** `in-thread`.
- **One item's text links to another:** `references`.
- **An item comes from another:** `excerpt-of` for a passage, `derived-from` for a summary.
- **A new item replaces an old one:** `supersedes`.

## Parts

An item that exists only for another, such as a comment or a receipt attached to an expense, is a **part**, and the item it belongs to is its **host**. **Would you look for it on its own?** If not, make it a part; if you would, as with a photo in an album, use another edge type. Listings still include parts: filter with `part eq false` to leave them out.

## Moving an item to the bin

An edge type's `cascade_on_delete` decides what the bin does across its edges:

- **`cascade`, on `parent-of`:** a parent takes its children with it, at every depth, and never the other way.
- **`with-hosts`, on `attached-to` and `comments-on`:** a part goes once its last host goes, and comes back when any host is restored.
- **`orphan`, on the other eight:** the other item stays active, and so does the edge.

So a note moved to the bin takes its child note and its comments, and leaves the book it's `about` where it is.

<BinCascade />

A registered edge type can also choose **`block`:** while such an edge holds an item, moving it to the bin is refused with `400 edge_constraint_violation`, naming the edges in `details.blocking_edges`. Delete the edge first. A purge is never blocked.

The rules behind this page are in the [edges](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/edges.md) chapter of the contract.
